body.en: EST II Math Level 2 previews calculus in two pieces: limits (what a function approaches, not just what it equals), and the derivative — defined directly as a limit, the same object every calculus course builds everything else on. This chapter also introduces, at the lightest possible level, what a differential equation even is.

\( \displaystyle\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=L \) means: as \( x \) approaches \( a \), \( f(x) \) approaches \( L \). For a polynomial or rational function with \( a \) in its domain, find the limit by direct substitution: \( \lim_{x\to a}f(x)=f(a) \).
If direct substitution gives \( \tfrac00 \), the limit is indeterminate, not automatically zero or undefined. For rational functions, factor and cancel the offending factor, then substitute again.

The derivative of \( f \) at \( x \), written \( f'(x) \), is defined as the limit of the difference quotient:

\[ f'(x)=\lim_{h\to0}\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}, \]

when that limit exists. It measures the instantaneous rate of change of \( f \) at \( x\) — the slope of the line tangent to \( f \)'s graph there.

By Definition 5.3, \[ f'(x)=\lim_{h\to0}\frac{(x+h)^2-x^2}{h}=\lim_{h\to0}\frac{x^2+2xh+h^2-x^2}{h}=\lim_{h\to0}\frac{2xh+h^2}{h}. \] For \( h\neq0 \) (which is all that matters for a limit as \( h\to0 \)), factor and cancel: \( \dfrac{2xh+h^2}{h}=\dfrac{h(2x+h)}{h}=2x+h \). So \[ f'(x)=\lim_{h\to0}(2x+h)=2x+0=2x. \quad\blacksquare \]

Using Theorem 5.1, find the slope of the tangent line to \( f(x)=x^2 \) at \( x=4 \).

\[ f'(4)=2(4)=8. \] (Numerically: the difference quotient at \( x=4 \) with tiny \( h \) — say \( h=0.001 \) — gives \( \approx8.001 \), confirming the limit is \( 8 \).)

body.en: A differential equation is an equation involving a function and its derivative(s). Solving one means finding the function(s) \( y \) that make the equation true — not a single number, but a whole function (usually a whole family of functions, differing by a constant).

label.en: Worked example 5.D — Verify a solution to a differential equation

body.en:
Show that \( y=x^2+5 \) solves \( \dfrac{dy}{dx}=2x \).

By Theorem 5.1, the derivative of \( x^2 \) is \( 2x \), and the derivative of the constant \( 5 \) is \( 0 \) (a constant never changes, so its instantaneous rate of change is \( 0 \)). So \[ \frac{dy}{dx}=2x+0=2x, \] exactly matching the equation. Any \( y=x^2+C \) for a constant \( C \) works the same way — this is the “whole family” Definition 5.4 mentions.

value.en: find the function(s) \( y \), not a number
